LE56 PREFACE. ——_¢—- To facilitate the taking of the census of Bengal, 1881, lists were compiled by the police of the villages and mouzas under each thana. As the only lists of the kind which previously existed were both imperfect and inaccurate, and considerable difficulty was at all times experi- enced in sorting letters received for the less known villages, it was determined to take advantage of the information contained in the manuscript census volumes, and to compile and print a village directory for the use of the post-office. With the sanction of the Director- General of Post-offices an establishment was entertained for copy- ing out the census lists, which were kindly lent for the purpose by the Deputy Superintendent of Census Operations. The villages were then arranged alphabetically, after which, with the assistance of local inform- ation, the namesof the post-offices from which each village receives its letters were entered. The Government of Bengal was pleased to oxpress its approval of the work, and to order a certain number of copies of the directory for the. use of its own offices. It also autho- rised the printing of the work at the Bengal Secretariat Press. Owing to the spread of education, and to improved communications, new post-offices are being constantly opened, and occasionally transfers of villages are made from one post-office to another. The directory has therefore been printed with a margin wide enough to admit of corree- tions. Whenever any change is made in the service of a village, the Superintendent of

Post-offices who authorises it will communicate a copy of the alteration to the Magistrate of the district, the post-office at the head-quarters of the district, as well as to all post-offices in the same district, and to the Manager, Dead Letter Office, Bengal; and the changes will be entered by these officials in the margin of their books. If therefore an officer belonging to another department of Government wishes to keep his copy corrected up to date, he can apply to the nearest post-office (if in the same district), and the Post- master or Sub-Postmaster will allow him to take a copy of the correc- tions entered %h the post-office volume. All copying work of the kind must be done by the applicant himself, or by some one whom he deputes for the purpose. ( 2 ) It is hoped that with the aid of the directory considerable improve- ment will be effected in the delivery of letters, which are frequently addressed to petty villages in the mofussil without the addition of eithor mouza or thana, and that the sorting of letters for rural post- offices generally will be more accurately done. Every effort has been made to make the directory as acourate and complete as possible. But the entries in the original census lists themselves were generally spelt very unscientifically, and in spite of all precautions some errors and omissions will doubtless be brought to light. The Postmaster-General, Bengal, will therefore feel much obliged by corrections being forwarded to him, along with full parti- culars of the village respecting which any mistake or omission may be discovered.
